artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Young–Fibonacci lattice YF is the graded lattice whose elements at rank n are the words (compositions) of 1's and 2's summing to n (with the empty word at rank 0), and whose covering relation w ⋖ w' (with rank(w') = rank(w) + 1) holds when w' is obtained from w either by prepending a 1, or by changing the leftmost run-prefix of 2's followed by changing a 1 just after that prefix into a 2 (equivalently: w' covers w iff w is obtained from w' by either deleting the leftmost 1 of w', or by changing a 2 of w' that lies in the leftmost block of consecutive 2's into a 1 and removing one such 2 — i.e., the standard Fomin/Stanley covering rule for the Young–Fibonacci lattice). A standard Young–Fibonacci tableau of shape w (rank n) is a saturated chain ∅ = w_0 ⋖ w_1 ⋖ ⋯ ⋖ w_n = w in YF.

Define SYFT to be the rooted tree whose vertices are all standard Young–Fibonacci tableaux (of all shapes, including the empty tableau as the root), with an edge between a tableau T of length n and a tableau T' of length n+1 whenever T' extends T by one additional cover. Equivalently, SYFT is the tree of upward paths from ∅ in the Young–Fibonacci lattice.

Forget all vertex labels, retaining only the abstract rooted (or unrooted) tree structure of SYFT. Determine the automorphism group of SYFT as an unlabeled tree.
artifact.status_search_result: A related question of Stanley (1988) on automorphisms of the Young–Fibonacci poset itself was resolved in the Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics, but the present question concerns the unlabeled tree of standard Young–Fibonacci tableaux (upward paths in the lattice), which is a distinct object. No published determination of the automorphism group of this tree was located, and the problem is listed among open problems on tableau combinatorics, indicating it remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: Solves Stanley's 1988 problem on the automorphism group of the Fibonacci poset.
status_evidence.claim: A related but distinct problem (automorphisms of the Fibonacci poset) was solved; the tree-of-tableaux automorphism question is separate.
